correctness.rationale: Exact μβ(B(0,r))=r^(β+1)/(β+1) yields failure of lower Q-regularity for Q<β+1, while polynomial ball weights are doubling. For λ>p+1, on every compact [a,b]⊂(0,1) the density is comparable to Lebesgue; adjacent-interval mean oscillations are O(h^((λ−1)/p)) with exponent strictly greater than one, and subdivision forces any Campanato element to be a.e. constant. Thus continuous embedding follows from finite total measure. If Q<λ≤p+1, a δ chosen between max(0,(λ−β−1)/p) and α=(λ−Q)/p exists because β+1>Q. f=x^δ has oscillation ≤C r^(pδ+β+1) near zero, and ≤C r^(p+1)x^(p(δ−1)+β) for x>2r; the two exponent cases ensure ≤C r^λ. Yet δ<α precludes a Hölder representative. These proofs apply to every p≥1 including p=1 and the λ=p+1 boundary if admissible; no finite numerical testing is needed.

final_claim: For x^βdx on [0,1] with β>0, 1<Q<β+1 and Q<λ<Q+p, the Campanato-to-Hölder embedding with exponent (λ−Q)/p holds precisely when λ>p+1, despite failure of lower Q-regularity, giving a model-family negative answer to the proposed doubling-only extension.
